input.strategy_title: Bundle an S3-compatible object store for disconnected installs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Pipelines and model serving both require S3-compatible object storage, but
disconnected customers frequently have none. Field teams work around this by
installing upstream MinIO ad hoc — unsupported, unpatched, and invisible to the
platform. We want a supported, bundled S3-compatible store that administrators
can enable for disconnected and PoC clusters. The leading candidate, MinIO, is
AGPL-3.0 licensed; redistribution terms must be cleared before any productization
work can ship, and the outcome may force a different upstream.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Legal review of redistributing the candidate object store (MinIO, AGPL-3.0) is completed and documented, including the derivative-work posture for operator integration. This clearance blocks all shipping work. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Administrators can enable a supported, bundled S3-compatible object store through the Platform Operator, with productized images and upgrade lifecycle. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Data Science Pipelines and model serving connection defaults can target the bundled store without manual endpoint configuration. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers enablement, sizing guidance, and the supported/unsupported boundary versus customer-provided storage. |

## Affected Components

- Platform Operator
- Data Science Pipelines
- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Replacing customer-provided S3 in connected environments
- Data migration tooling between stores

## Open Questions

1. If AGPL terms cannot be satisfied for our distribution model, the fallback
   candidate is an Apache-2.0 alternative (e.g. SeaweedFS) — acceptable, but it
   restarts image productization.

# Legal clearance for redistributing the candidate object store (MinIO, AGPL-3.0)

## Description

This investigation resolves the gating unknown for the entire strategy:
whether MinIO, licensed AGPL-3.0, can be legally redistributed as part of the
product — including the derivative-work posture for integrating it with the
Platform Operator (bundling the container image and deploying it
operator-managed). The outcome determines which upstream all productization
work targets: MinIO if terms are satisfiable, or the documented Apache-2.0
fallback candidate (e.g. SeaweedFS) if they are not. HLR-1 states this
clearance blocks all shipping work.

## Scope

- Obtain a legal review of redistributing MinIO under AGPL-3.0 within the
  product's distribution model (container image redistribution plus
  operator-driven deployment on customer clusters).
- Document the derivative-work posture for operator integration — whether
  deploying/managing MinIO from the Platform Operator creates obligations.
- If the terms cannot be satisfied for the distribution model, confirm the
  Apache-2.0 fallback candidate and record the selection decision.
- Deliverable: a documented clearance decision naming the object store
  upstream that all downstream productization work targets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The legal review is completed and documented, covering redistribution terms
  for the candidate store and the derivative-work posture for operator
  integration (HLR-1).
- A decision is recorded: MinIO cleared for redistribution, or the Apache-2.0
  fallback candidate selected as the target upstream.
- The decision is communicated such that downstream productization work
  (midstream repo, image productization, operator enablement) can be scoped
  against the selected store.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): fully covered — this epic performs and documents the legal
  review of redistributing the candidate object store.

## Notes

This is a human legal/governance decision, not a technical spike: the answer
does not exist in any readable artifact and must be produced by legal review.
Routing should assign it to a person, not an automated investigation.

# Midstream repo onboarding for the selected S3-compatible object store

## Description

Creates the midstream repository under opendatahub-io for the S3-compatible
object store selected by the legal clearance (MinIO, or the Apache-2.0
fallback if AGPL terms cannot be satisfied), so that productized images and
the upgrade lifecycle can be built and maintained under platform support.
This is a prerequisite for all image productization work — the code and
builds need a repo to live in.

## Scope

- Fork/import the selected object store upstream into a midstream repository
  under opendatahub-io.
- Establish branching, versioning, and rebase/upgrade conventions consistent
  with other productized midstream components.
- Wire the repo into the standard midstream hygiene (CI triggers, OWNERS,
  retention policy) per existing conventions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A midstream repository exists under opendatahub-io for the object store
  named by the legal clearance decision.
- The repo tracks the selected upstream version and follows the established
  midstream conventions used by other productized components.
- The repo is ready to receive build pipeline onboarding and image
  productization changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): prerequisite for "productized images and upgrade lifecycle" —
  the midstream repo is where productized images are built and maintained.

## Gate Dependency

This epic is gated by the legal clearance investigation: if AGPL terms cannot
be satisfied for MinIO, the onboarded upstream changes to the Apache-2.0
fallback candidate. The epic's structure and deliverable are unchanged; only
the target upstream is rewritten.

# License validation of the selected object store and its transitive dependencies

## Description

Runs automated license scanning over the S3-compatible object store selected
by the legal clearance (its source and container image) and its transitive
dependencies, producing the compliance evidence that supplements the AGPL
legal review. This validates that no transitive dependency introduces a
license conflict with the product's distribution terms before productization
work ships.

## Scope

- Run the standard license scanning tooling over the selected store's source
  tree and container image, including the full transitive dependency graph.
- Record license findings; identify any restricted or conflicting licenses.
- Escalate any conflicts with proposed remediation (dependency swap, upgrade,
  exclusion) for legal/product sign-off.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Scan results are documented for the selected object store and its
  transitive dependencies.
- No unresolved license conflict blocks productization of the selected store;
  any conflict is escalated with a documented remediation path.
- The evidence is archived so it can back the documented legal clearance and
  the supported/unsupported boundary documentation.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): contributes the automated compliance evidence behind the
  documented legal review.
- HLR-2 (P0): gates shipping of productized images — if licenses fail, the
  dependency set changes and the productization approach is affected.

## Gate Dependency

Gated by the legal clearance investigation: the scan target is the store
selected by that decision. If the fallback candidate is selected, the scan is
rewritten to target it — the epic's work is identical in shape.

# Productize and enable the bundled S3-compatible object store via the Platform Operator

## Description

Builds the productized container image of the selected S3-compatible object
store in its midstream repository and adds Platform Operator support so that
administrators can enable a supported, bundled S3-compatible store — with
productized images and upgrade lifecycle — on disconnected and PoC clusters.
This is the core delivery of the strategy: a supported alternative to the
unsupported ad hoc upstream MinIO installs field teams currently perform.

## Scope

- Productize the selected store's container image in the midstream repository
  (pinned, product-versioned, built through the onboarded build pipeline).
- Platform Operator support for enabling the bundled store as an opt-in
  capability: deployment, configuration, and lifecycle management.
- Upgrade lifecycle: version upgrades of the bundled store handled by the
  operator without manual reinstall or data loss.
- Ensure enabling the bundled store has no impact on customer-provided S3 in
  connected environments (explicitly out of scope per the strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The productized image of the selected store builds green through the
  onboarded Konflux build pipeline.
- On a disconnected cluster, an administrator can enable the bundled
  S3-compatible object store through the Platform Operator; the store comes
  up and serves S3-compatible endpoints (HLR-2).
- The bundled store carries a productized image and upgrade lifecycle:
  operator-driven upgrades complete without manual reinstall.
- Enabling the bundled store is opt-in and can be disabled/rolled back
  without affecting customer-provided storage configurations.
- A pinned image digest for the productized store image is available for
  consumption by deployment/packaging configuration.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): primary coverage — administrator enablement via the Platform
  Operator with productized images and upgrade lifecycle.

## Gate Dependency

Gated by the legal clearance investigation (HLR-1 blocks all shipping work):
if AGPL terms cannot be satisfied for MinIO, this epic is rewritten to
productize and enable the Apache-2.0 fallback store instead. Scope and
structure are unchanged; the targeted upstream and its image differ.

# Data Science Pipelines connection defaults for the bundled object store

## Description

Makes Data Science Pipelines target the bundled S3-compatible object store by
default when it is enabled, so that pipeline artifact storage works on
disconnected clusters without manual endpoint configuration. The Data Science
Pipelines architecture already depends on S3-compatible object storage for
artifacts; this epic wires the default to the platform-bundled store's
exposure (endpoint and credentials handling) provided by the operator
enablement.

## Scope

- Default the Data Science Pipelines storage configuration to the bundled
  store's endpoint and credentials when the bundled store is enabled on the
  cluster.
- Require no manual endpoint configuration for pipeline artifact storage
  against the bundled store.
- Preserve explicit/customer-provided S3 configuration: where a
  customer-provided store is configured, it takes precedence over the
  bundled default.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With the bundled store enabled, Data Science Pipelines uses it for
  artifact storage with no manual endpoint configuration (HLR-3).
- Where customer-provided S3 is configured, pipelines continue to target it —
  the bundled default does not override explicit configuration.
- Dashboard-managed pipeline storage settings continue to work against the
  bundled store defaults (passive validation of the Dashboard component: no
  Dashboard code change, existing storage configuration surfaces keep
  functioning).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): Data Science Pipelines half of connection defaults targeting
  the bundled store.

# Model serving connection defaults for the bundled object store

## Description

Makes model serving connection defaults target the bundled S3-compatible
object store when it is enabled, so that model artifacts are pulled from the
bundled store on disconnected clusters without manual endpoint
configuration. The defaults build on the store exposure (endpoint and
credentials handling) provided by the operator enablement of the bundled
store.

## Scope

- Default model serving storage configuration (model artifact location) to
  the bundled store's endpoint and credentials when the bundled store is
  enabled on the cluster.
- Require no manual endpoint configuration for serving models from the
  bundled store.
- Preserve explicit/customer-provided S3 configuration: where a
  customer-provided store is configured, it takes precedence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With the bundled store enabled, model serving retrieves model artifacts
  from the bundled store with no manual endpoint configuration (HLR-3).
- Where customer-provided S3 is configured, model serving continues to
  target it — the bundled default does not override explicit configuration.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): model serving half of connection defaults targeting the
  bundled store.
